extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, SBE-FPs, FFE administrators, QHP issuers, web-broker/DE partners, and other health coverage stakeholders providing comments on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and regulatory text proposing a set of changes to Exchange operations, plan standards, auditing/measurement requirements, and related administrative burdens for the 2027 benefit year; the page solicits comments and provides cost/burden estimates and implementation guidance for States, issuers, and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated exemption processing system cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated one-time development cost and staff hours to build an automated exemption processing system (detailed per-occupation estimates and totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides line-item labor estimates: e.g., Business Analysts ~600 hours @ $94.88/hr = $56,928; Database/Network Admins ~200 hours @ $103.34/hr = $20,668; Project Manager ~160 hours @ $96.88/hr = $15,501. Testing/QC: Computer Systems Analysts ~120 hours @ $99.80/hr = $11,976; Compliance Officers ~80 hours @ $75.40/hr = $6,032. Implementation/training: Management Analysts ~80 hours @ $97.30/hr = $7,784; Eligibility Interviewers ~40 hours @ $49.52/hr = $1,981. Combined system development ~1,360 staff hours; testing ~200 hours; implementation/training ~120 hours. Total estimated one-time cost in PY 2026 = ~$160,790 per State (total $643,160 for four State Exchanges). Notes: estimates vary with state infrastructure (modern vs legacy), customizations, and integration complexity. The agency requests comments on estimated application numbers, consumer and Exchange time burdens, and opportunities to reduce burden (automation, streamlined processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of Exchange Network Adequacy Standards (§155.1050(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to eliminate federal requirements that State Exchanges/SBE-FPs establish quantitative time/distance standards and to stop requiring quantitative network adequacy reviews prior to QHP certification; instead require assurances that QHPs provide sufficient access consistent with §§156.230(a)(1)(ii),(a)(1)(iii) or proposed §156.236(a) for non-network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States would have greater flexibility to regulate and review network adequacy based on local market conditions. HHS recognizes many States already have robust standards. Anticipated impacts: maintain regulatory burden on 22 State Exchanges and 1 SBE-FP for PY 2027, estimated cost impact $1,560,780 beginning PY 2027. Potential increased administrative burden on multi-state issuers due to varying state frameworks and a risk of decreased access to care if State standards are less protective than Federal framework. The agency solicits comments on these impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Program Integrity and Oversight Requirements (§155.1200) — SEIPM substitution for annual external audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to permit State Exchanges to satisfy certain annual independent external programmatic audit requirements by completing the proposed annual SEIPM program process, reducing duplication between SEIPM and §155.1200 audit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected to reduce audit contract costs for State Exchanges that operate their own eligibility/enrollment platforms. HHS projects a ~30% reduction in annual audit cost (~$45,000 per State Exchange based on ~$150,000 average audit cost), totaling ~$990,000 across 22 State Exchanges beginning 2027. However, adopting SEIPM introduces new burdens associated with completing SEIPM and related Corrective Action Plan (CAP) processes. The agency requests State Exchanges' feedback on annual programmatic audit costs and the proposed burden reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) requirements (§§155.1600–155.1650)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to implement PIIA improper payment measurement for State Exchanges, requiring measurement of improper payments related to eligibility/APTC determinations and submission of Corrective Action Plans responsive to findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational assumptions and cost estimates: average cost per sample = $499; planned sample sizes by State range from 50 to 250, yielding per-respondent costs ~$24,950–$124,750. Total State Exchange costs to produce proposed information and undergo review estimated at $1,097,800. CAP development estimated up to 1,000 hours or $97,300 per State Exchange; aggregate annual burden for up to 22 respondents = up to 22,000 hours and $2,140,600. HHS anticipates 6 FTEs for SEIPM activities/contract management at $376,075 per FTE (derived from a $183,500 base salary doubled for fringe/overhead), totaling $2,256,450 annually. HHS contracting costs estimated at $19.5M annually (data collection, automated review systems, statistical methodology, appeals, improper payment estimation, reports, IT). Total annual expected cost across States/HHS = ~$24.8M. The agency will submit the information collection to OMB for approval after future rulemaking on CAP processes; comments requested on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE and SBE-FP User Fee Rates (§156.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed FFE user fee rate of 2.5% and SBE-FP user fee rate of 2.0% for the 2027 benefit year, unchanged from 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because rates are unchanged, user fee transfers from issuers to the Federal Government are expected to remain consistent with prior estimates. HHS expects available collections to be sufficient to fund Exchange operations through 2027 at proposed rates. The agency seeks comment on these impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Health Benefits — prohibition on routine non-pediatric dental as an EHB (§156.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to revise §156.115(d) to prohibit issuers from including routine non-pediatric dental services as an EHB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency does not anticipate immediate costs to Federal/State Governments, issuers, or enrollees because no State has yet added routine non-pediatric dental as an EHB under the earlier policy. Reinstating the prohibition avoids potential premium increases and network expansion costs that issuers might incur if required to cover these services as EHB (although issuers could instead contract with dental vendors). The typicality standard at §156.111(b)(2)(ii) limits premium impacts from additions to EHB-benchmark plans. The agency acknowledges potential health outcome impacts from limiting non-pediatric dental coverage and notes States may address oral health via non-EHB mandates or other mechanisms. The agency solicits comments on impacts and any other considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Year Terms for Catastrophic Plans (§§156.130 and 156.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to permit catastrophic plans to have multi-year contract periods (minimum 2 years) rather than annual renewals, with the ability to adjust premiums and benefits during the term consistent with applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended benefits: increased predictability for eligible consumers, reduced re-enrollment administrative burden, potential for plans to offer preventive services before deductible via value-based designs, possible market stability gains. Potential downsides: reduced consumer flexibility to switch plans, conservative issuer pricing leading to higher initial premiums, uncertainty about effects on risk selection and enrollment composition, actuarial challenges pricing up to 10-year terms, and unknown demand. States and Federal government would face review/approval costs. Agency seeks comments on issuer participation, operational impacts, market segmentation, transfer effects, premium impacts, Federal PTC expenditures, and data to quantify impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Sharing parameters for Bronze and Catastrophic Plans (§§156.136 and 156.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to add §156.136 to permit individual market bronze plans to exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing in order to achieve an AV within the standard bronze de minimis, and to revise §156.155(a)(3) to require catastrophic plans to provide no benefits until reaching 130% of the annual limitation on cost sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: issuers may offer one or more increased-annual-limitation bronze plans only if they also offer at least one bronze plan that meets the standard annual limitation. Expected effects: could incentivize catastrophic enrollment by permitting lower-premium catastrophic plans, but would raise expected out-of-pocket costs by up to 30% for catastrophic plan enrollees incurring significant costs; bronze enrollees could face larger increases. Provides consumers additional bronze plan design options (e.g., lower deductibles/lower premiums). The agency requests comments on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of Standardized Plan Options (§§155.20, 155.205(b)(1), 155.220(c)(3)(i)(H), 156.201, 156.265(b)(3)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to discontinue the regulatory suite establishing standardized plan options and to cease differential display of standardized plans on HealthCare.gov and DE pathways effective PY 2027; would remove the definition and all related requirements and stop annual design/publication of standardized plans in Payment Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers may continue to offer formerly standardized plans (unchanged or modified cost sharing) at their discretion. If an issuer discontinues a standardized plan, enrollees would be crosswalked per §155.335(j). Modifying cost sharing may render a plan a new plan (new plan ID) unless State permits greater changes consistent with the definition of “plan” at §144.103 and uniform modification exceptions at §147.106(e). Differential display removal by HHS reduces burden on issuers; DE/web-broker/QHP issuer enrollment partners would need minor platform modifications to decommission differential display features, but burden is expected to be minimal (reverting functionality to prior state is less burdensome than adding new features). The agency references additional literature in the preamble and seeks comment on impact estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of Non-Standardized Plan Option Limits and Exceptions (§156.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to discontinue non-standardized plan option limits and the exceptions process at §156.202, while permitting issuers to continue offering chronic and high-cost condition plans (or other non-standardized options) with same or modified cost sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer options mirror standardized-plan discontinuation: discontinuation leads to crosswalks under §155.335(j); continuing with same cost sharing allows auto-reenrollment; modifying cost sharing may create a new plan ID unless State treats modifications as the same plan per §144.103 and uniform modification rules under §147.106(e). Expected outcome: reduced regulatory complexity and burden while minimizing consumer/issuer disruption. The agency seeks comment on impact estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider Access Standards and Effective Provider Access Review Program (§155.1050 and §156.230)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal at §155.1050(d) to allow FFE States (including plan-management States that elect to do so) to conduct provider access reviews for issuers' plans (network and non-network) if the State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity by satisfying criteria to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program (§155.1050(d)(2)–(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State does not elect to conduct reviews or cannot demonstrate sufficient authority/technical capacity, HHS would continue network adequacy reviews under §156.230 for network plans and provider access reviews for non-network plans. The agency will continue to collect network adequacy data (time/distance and appointment wait time) from all FFE issuers either for Federal reviews or to make standardized data available to States with Effective Provider Access Review Programs. Rationale: prior years' experience shows one-size-fits-all network adequacy reviews are unsatisfactory; providers in certain specialties and remote areas can be hard to source/contract. The agency seeks comment and data to inform implementation and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network adequacy data collection requirements (time/distance and appointment wait times)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued collection of issuer-submitted network adequacy data including quantitative time and distance measures and appointment wait time data from all FFE issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data will be used either to conduct Federal network adequacy reviews in FFE States that do not elect or cannot demonstrate capacity to conduct their own reviews, or to provide standardized data to States determined to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program to assist state-level analyses. The preamble notes variation in local market conditions and specialty provider availability (e.g., allergy/immunology, behavioral health, gastroenterology) and implies that collected data should reflect those local differences to inform reviews. The agency requests comments on the proposal and the adequacy of the data and criteria.
